newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling opens week firmer against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling opens week firmer against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened on Monday slightly stronger against the dollar as flows of U.S. currency into Kenya from tea and coffee exporters increased, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.78 against the dollar from 55.88 on Friday, while on the pound it was posted at 91.96 from 92.05.
Dealers said interbank activity was high as dollar inflows from exports had increased, causing the shilling to gain.
Last week saw an increase in demand for dollars from oil companies causing the shilling to weaken against the dollar.

Dealers said last week's shilling weakening was temporary as it could not be sustained due to lack of importer demand. They expect 55.70 level to be the next resistance level for the shilling against the dollar.
